verdict.rationale: OpenTofu keeps infrastructure definitions in human-readable configuration files that users can version and share. It stays a drop-in, Terraform-compatible, truly open-source tool, so configurations stay portable and users can move between tools easily, as community migration reports confirm. Missing for 10: documented export of state data in an open format such as JSON, an explicit data-export or exit procedure, and evidence that all user data (state, plans, encrypted artifacts) can be extracted in open formats.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: lets you define both cloud and on-premises resources in human-readable configuration files that you can version, reuse, and share
It serves as a drop-in replacement for Terraform, preserving your existing workflows and configurations.
Truly open source - under a well-known and widely-accepted license that companies can trust, that won't suddenly change in the future
Fortunately using OpenTofu is just s/terraform/opentofu/g at this point.
